  - text: CLASS 10 · STATISTICS
  - heading "Median from an Ogive" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Find the median of grouped data using two equivalent graphical constructions and compare with the grouped median formula.
  - navigation: 18 min INTERMEDIATE CONCEPT statistics
  - complementary:
    - text: KEY IDEA
    - paragraph: The median splits the data into two equal parts (N/2 each). Both less-than and more-than ogives give the same median.
  - main:
    - heading "1 ) DATA (Grouped Frequency Distribution)" [level=2]

    - heading "2 ) DUAL OGIVE (Less-than & More-than on same axes)" [level=2]
    - checkbox "Less-than ogive" [checked]
    - text: Less-than ogive
    - checkbox "More-than ogive" [checked]
    - text: More-than ogive
    - button "Reset points":
      - img
      - text: Reset points
    - img "Dual ogive median construction": N/2 = 25 Intersection (29.17, 25) 0 10 20 30 40 50 60
    - article:
      - text: Read-off from Less-than ogive
      - paragraph: At cumulative frequency N/2 = 25
      - strong: x (Median) = 29.17
    - article:
      - text: Intersection of ogives
      - strong: (29.17, 25)
      - paragraph: Median = 29.17
    - article:
      - text: Read-off from More-than ogive
      - paragraph: At cumulative frequency N/2 = 25
      - strong: x (Median) = 29.17
    - complementary:
      - text: Why do both constructions agree?
      - paragraph: At the median, half the observations lie below and half lie above, so both curves meet the N/2 guide at the same x-value.
    - heading "3 ) GROUPED MEDIAN FORMULA" [level=2]
    - strong: Median = l + ((N/2 − cᶠ) / f) h
    - paragraph: l = lower boundary, cᶠ = cumulative frequency before median class, f = frequency, h = class width
    - text: "N/2 = 25 Median class: 20 – 30 l=20, cᶠ=14, f=12, h=10 Median = 20 + (25 − 14)/12 × 10 = 29.17"
    - mark: Median (Formula) ≈ 29.17
    - heading "4 ) COMPARISON" [level=2]

      - text: All methods agree because they derive from the same grouped distribution.
